title: Squad state file
description: Per-squad state the Lead owns and writes. Carries only what Orca does not already model; activity, lineage, and agent status come from `orca worktree ps` and the orchestration Run.

task_id.description: The squad's orchestration task id (`task_...`, from task-create at spawn). Checkpoint gates target this task.

run_id.description: The squad's orchestration Run id (`run_...`). The Lead `run-use`s it to become its coordinator; the board reads gate/inbox state from it.

lead_wt.description: The Lead's worktree id. Lets the Lead fan out more workers under itself via bin/commands/add-role.sh (parallel Builders, on-demand roles).

members.description: The squad's full roster — one entry per member, 1:1 with a worktree. The single source of truth for who is in the squad and what each owns; worktrees[] and assignments[] are DERIVED from it. Enough to recreate the squad (respawn) and to answer 'who was doing what' after a restart. Live status (working/idle) is NOT stored here — it comes from `worker-states` at render time.

role.description: lead | thinker | builder | reviewer | tester | researcher.

suffix.description: Distinguishes members of the same role (e.g. `checkout`, `t2`); empty for a base role.

wt.description: The member's worktree id (the key — one member per worktree).

owns.description: What this member is responsible for — a Thinker's plan file(s), a Builder's unit slug(s), the Tester's env. A list, so a Thinker can own several plans.

for.description: (Builders) the Thinker scope this worker reports to; drives Builder→Thinker question routing.

host.description: The saved env this member runs on (empty = default host). Recorded so a respawn recreates it in place.

account.description: The account id the member runs on (backend `account-list`). Missing = the agent's default login (the first account-list line for its agent), so old squads keep working.

fallback.description: True when the picker put the member on one of its role's fallback models rather than the role's own. Stored, not derived: the roster can change after spawn.

worktrees.description: DERIVED from members[].wt (every worktree id this squad created). Kept so bin/commands/close-squad.sh and other readers that just need the ids don't have to walk members[]. Do not write directly on a squad that uses members[] — add-member/remove-member maintain it.

repo.description: Repo selector the squad was spawned with (replication input for respawn).

host.description: Saved env the squad was spawned on, or null for the default host (replication input).

framing.description: The operator's framing sentence that seeded the squad (replication input).

start.description: The start the Studio named at spawn (spawn-squad.sh --start); the feature squad's Thinker sees it in its first start prompt. Null = the Thinker picks by its Start triage.

debrief.description: The Lead's short debrief of the squad (set out to do / shipped with PR numbers / learned / still open / cost), written with set-debrief. set-status done refuses without one. It rides in the doc, so the archive keeps it. Absent = none yet.

units.description: The plan's work items — the durable queue that makes a dropped handoff recoverable. The Lead records a unit `planned` when the Thinker hands off, `dispatched` (with the Builder's worktree id) when it fans out a Builder, `done` when complete. `cancelled` (via cancel-unit, through close-role.sh --cancel) means the work folded elsewhere or was dropped: the sweep never restarts or questions it, and ready-units counts it for a dependent only when its work landed somewhere (folded into the dependent, into a done unit, or into a merged PR). watch.sh and the board derive their WORK ITEMS view from this: a `planned` unit with no Builder and a `dispatched` unit whose worktree is GONE are the two failures surfaced.

slug.description: Short unit identifier (e.g. `checkout`); matches the Builder's suffix.

superseded_by.description: (cancelled units) what the work folded into: a unit slug, or `PR#<n>`. Absent = the work was dropped, not folded — dependents stay blocked until the Lead drops the dep or replans.

into_merged.description: (cancelled units with a PR# superseded_by) true once the sweep sees that PR merged — dependents unblock. Set by set-into-merged; absent reads as false.

builder_wt.description: The worktree id of the Builder working this unit (set at dispatch); empty while planned.

plan.description: The plan file this unit came from, so units stay grouped when a Thinker owns several plans.

hold.description: Held planned work: ready-units and ready pokes skip it. With hold_reason, set-unit-hold off releases it; without a reason, the operator promotes it explicitly at triage. Absent = not held.

hold_by.description: Where a reasonless hold came from, set by register-plan: plan = a HELD line (released when the line drops HELD and the plan is registered again), parked = an add-unit --hold follow-up a plan line adopted. Absent on older holds.

hold_reason.description: Operator freeze reason, set by set-unit-hold on --why on planned units; the board shows held · <reason>. set-unit-hold off removes it. Absent on parked follow-ups and plan HELD lines.

revalidated.description: U3: on a unit held with hold_reason `revalidate after resume`, set by approve-plan of its plan (approved again after a suspend's resume); the next register-plan of that plan releases the hold. set-unit-hold off and a new resume hold remove it.

urgent.description: Unit the operator needs first: its Builder ranks ahead of every non-urgent candidate and starts even at max_builders. Set by set-unit-urgent on (a planned or dispatched unit); off releases it. Absent = not urgent.

urgent_why.description: Why the unit was marked urgent (set-unit-urgent --why). Absent when unmarked or no reason was given.

lane.description: Lane from the plan line's `Lane:` field (register-plan). Absent = normal.

title.description: The unit line's title from the plan (register-plan), shown in the board's unit overlay; updated when the plan is registered again.

about.description: What the unit does: the plan's `What:` text (register-plan, 1200 characters at most) or add-unit --about. Absent = not stored.

done.description: The plan's `Done:` line for the unit (register-plan, 400 characters at most). Absent = not stored.

check.description: The plan's `Check:` line for the unit (register-plan, 400 characters at most). Absent = not stored.

lane_rule.description: The shared lane rule id from `Lane: light (rule: <id>)`. Absent when the plan line names none.

wait_on.description: Waits recorded by wait-on / a plan's `— blocks:` line: dep (a same-squad slug, or `<squad>/<slug>` for an ext dep) -> why. The dep is also in deps/ext_deps; the loop pauses the Builder of a dispatched unit until each is done. register-plan keeps these deps; wait-off removes the entry. Absent = none.

wait_until.description: Epoch seconds. Set (set-unit-wait) when no account/model is free for the unit's Builder; ready-units skips the unit until it passes; cleared when the Builder starts (set-unit-status dispatched).

deps.description: Same-squad unit slugs this unit waits on (the Thinker's DAG); ready-units holds it until each is `done`.

ext_deps.description: Other squads' units this unit waits on, as `<squad>/<slug>` in the same label. ready-units holds it until each is `done` in squads/<squad>.json or an archive/<squad>-*.json; a missing squad or unit blocks (fail-closed) until the Lead runs drop-ext-dep. Absent = none.

tier.description: The Thinker's Builder tier (add-unit --tier); absent reads as hard.

escalated.description: Set when set-unit-tier raised the unit standard -> hard.

pr.description: The PR number the unit's Builder opened (set-unit-pr).

plan_unit.description: The unit's id in its plan (`U1`, `U24b`), set by register-plan; a re-run matches on (plan, plan_unit) so a renamed title keeps its slug.

leftovers.description: Worktrees that couldn't be removed without losing work (close-role keeps one instead of force-deleting; the sweep removes it once clean and pushed/merged, close-squad refuses to archive while one is unsafe). Nothing here is ever force-deleted by automation.

wt.description: The worktree id (upsert key; rekey-member follows it, add-member clears it when the worktree is reused).

branch.description: The branch the worktree was on.

reason.description: Why it was kept (e.g. `uncommitted changes`, `unpushed commits`, `unknown (probe failed)`).

waits_on.description: What it waits on (e.g. `PR#19717`, a unit slug, or `the Lead/operator decision`).

unit.description: The unit slug whose Builder left it, when known.

files.description: Up to the first 20 uncommitted file names.

unpushed.description: Commits on HEAD not on any remote.

devenv.description: Where a shared env is reachable (URL/address + note), or null if none. The Lead records it when a role reports an env is up, so everyone uses that one env instead of starting their own. Project-agnostic: null for projects with no shared env.

cleanup.description: Teardown commands to run when the squad closes (bin/commands/close-squad.sh runs each). Project-agnostic: any role that starts something DETACHED (a dev server, a docker stack, a watcher) that removing its worktree won't stop registers how to stop it here, so it doesn't outlive the squad. dev-studio never interprets the commands.

assignments.description: DERIVED from members[] (each Builder with a `for`): which worker, on what unit, owned by which Thinker. Makes Builder->Thinker routing durable, which matters once a squad has more than one Thinker. Maintained by add-member/remove-member; don't write directly.

unit.description: Short description of what it's working on.

thinker.description: The owning Thinker's scope (e.g. `authbug`); its questions route there.

autonomy.description: Autonomy mode: checkpoints (stop at gates) or lfg (fire-and-forget, decide-log-continue).

type.description: Squad type: a feature squad builds a topic; a testing squad runs the env, intakes manual-testing observations, and fixes issues.

status.description: Semantic status the board reads. `waiting-on-you` = a question reached the operator (the Lead pinged); `failed` = spawn aborted partway (kept visible so it can be torn down, not deleted); `suspended` = worktrees removed by /ds-suspend, resumable.

waiting_on_you.description: Pending questions mirrored from the Run inbox for the board's blocked-first queue.

blocking.description: true = work is stalled (pushes); false = soft, waits on the board.

suggestion.description: The asker's suggested answer (ask-operator.sh requires it); /ds-q offers it as 'Accept'.

card_wt.description: The worktree whose card carries the NEEDS YOU note; resolve-question clears it.

options.description: Answer options offered to the operator.

pr.description: The PR the question is about (ask-operator.sh --pr); the loop closes the question if the PR stops being ready.

doc_path.description: A document the question links (ask-operator.sh --doc; a plan-* question gets its plan by the id rule): path relative to the state root, `<label>/squads/<file>.md` or `<label>/archive/<file>.md`. The board shows it as Open plan / Open doc.

source.description: "picker" when the entry mirrors a terminal AskUserQuestion picker (bin/hooks/picker-hook.sh); absent for questions raised through ask-operator.sh by an agent.

tool_use_id.description: (picker entries) the AskUserQuestion tool_use_id, so the post hook and the sweep can tell whether the picker is still open.

transcript_path.description: (picker entries) the agent transcript carrying the picker's tool_result once it is answered or dismissed.

picker_answerable.description: (picker entries) true only for a single-question, single-select picker — the only shape the board can answer by keystroke.

approved_plans.description: Plans the operator approved (approve-plan); the Lead dispatches only units of an approved plan.

revoked_plans.description: Plan approvals taken back (revoke-plan), oldest first; approving the plan again keeps the history.

plan.description: The plan's canonical path, as approved_plans held it.

by.description: DS_WHO, else the caller's role, else "operator".

proposed_squads.description: A testing squad's proposed fix squads (propose-squad), for operator approval.

lfg_assumptions.description: Assumptions an lfg squad logged instead of blocking, shown on the board for after-the-fact review.
